What to track: Total sleep time per 24 hours from wrist actigraphy
Target / threshold: 8.5-hour sleep opportunity recommended; NASA does not set a minimum total sleep time
Related risk(s): Risk from Inadequate Sleep and Irregular Schedules
Related countermeasure(s): Circadian LED lighting; Designated relaxation and self-care time
Issue / consequence if out of range: Cumulative sleep debt, daytime sleepiness, slower reaction time, poorer decision-making and mood, reduced recovery.
Operational impact: Higher error rates on critical tasks; degraded EVA, docking and flight performance.
Notes: The 8.5 h figure is the scheduled opportunity, not a measured sleep floor.

What to track: Bedtime, wake time and night-to-night variability
Target / threshold: Keep timing consistent; avoid critical tasks during the 1-7 AM circadian nadir
Related risk(s): Risk from Inadequate Sleep and Irregular Schedules
Issue / consequence if out of range: Circadian desynchronization, poor sleep quality, insomnia, daytime fatigue and mood disturbance.
Operational impact: Alertness misaligned with critical task times; impaired judgment and teamwork.
Notes: Circadian entrainment requires consistent sleep timing day to day.

What to track: Sleep efficiency = total sleep time / time in bed
Target / threshold: No NASA numeric limit; track trend
Related risk(s): Risk from Inadequate Sleep and Irregular Schedules
Issue / consequence if out of range: Fragmented, non-restorative sleep and reduced recovery.
Operational impact: Lower vigilance and cognitive performance; fatigue accumulation.

What to track: Time from lights-out to sleep onset
Target / threshold: No NASA numeric limit; track trend
Related risk(s): Risk from Inadequate Sleep and Irregular Schedules
Issue / consequence if out of range: Difficulty falling asleep and shortened sleep.
Operational impact: Reduced total sleep and next-day performance decline.

What to track: Wake after sleep onset and number of awakenings
Target / threshold: No NASA numeric limit; track trend
Related risk(s): Risk from Inadequate Sleep and Irregular Schedules
Issue / consequence if out of range: Frequent awakenings and poor sleep continuity.
Operational impact: Daytime fatigue and attention lapses.

What to track: Illuminance and RGB light from wrist sensors; melanopic EDI estimate
Target / threshold: Daytime at least 250 melanopic EDI lux; pre-sleep 8 +/- 2; sleep period at most 0.02 lux
Related risk(s): Risk from Inadequate Sleep and Irregular Schedules; Risk of Behavioral Changes and Psychiatric Disorders
Issue / consequence if out of range: Circadian misalignment, melatonin suppression, delayed sleep onset and poor sleep quality; low daytime light reduces alertness.
Operational impact: Shifted sleep-wake cycle, fatigue, mood and performance effects.
Notes: Melanopic values are estimated from photopic and RGB channels.

What to track: Core temperature time series and circadian phase
Target / threshold: No NASA numeric limit; track circadian trend
Related risk(s): Risk from Inadequate Sleep and Irregular Schedules
Issue / consequence if out of range: Thermoregulatory strain and disrupted circadian rhythm and sleep timing.
Operational impact: Heat stress during exercise or EVA; poor sleep.
Notes: Measured with a forehead heat-flux sensor.

What to track: Scheduled sleep opportunity, duty hours, exercise and task timing
Target / threshold: 8.5 h sleep period plus 2 h pre-sleep and 1.5 h post-sleep; limits on duty and workload
Monitoring source: Sleep logs and questionnaires; crew schedule
Related risk(s): Risk from Inadequate Sleep and Irregular Schedules; Risk of Behavioral Changes and Psychiatric Disorders
Issue / consequence if out of range: Fatigue, burnout, circadian disruption and sleep loss.
Operational impact: Critical-task errors; degraded crew performance and safety.
Notes: NASA requires that schedule limits be established.

What to track: Session completion, duration, type and weekly consistency
Target / threshold: 1.5 hours per day, 6-7 days per week (ISS practice)
Threshold basis: ISS operational practice (NASA Human Research Program)
Monitoring source: ARED; CEVIS cycle ergometer and T2 treadmill
Related risk(s): Risk of Reduced Cardiorespiratory and Musculoskeletal Fitness; Risk of Spaceflight-Induced Bone Changes
Related countermeasure(s): Resistance training 1.5 hours per day; Aerobic exercise 1.5 hours per day
Issue / consequence if out of range: Muscle atrophy, bone loss, aerobic deconditioning and reduced cardiovascular capacity.
Operational impact: Difficulty with EVA tasks, emergency egress and post-flight recovery; higher injury risk.
Notes: NASA-STD-3001 sets outcome thresholds, not a daily duration.

What to track: Resistive versus aerobic minutes and sessions
Target / threshold: Include both resistance and aerobic exercise each week
Monitoring source: ARED; CEVIS cycle ergometer and T2 treadmill
Related risk(s): Risk of Reduced Cardiorespiratory and Musculoskeletal Fitness
Related countermeasure(s): Resistance training 1.5 hours per day; Aerobic exercise 1.5 hours per day
Issue / consequence if out of range: Imbalance between strength and aerobic fitness; incomplete protection of bone and muscle.
Operational impact: Reduced EVA capability and injury resilience.

What to track: Applied load and repetitions on the resistive device
Target / threshold: No NASA numeric target; track training volume and progression
Related risk(s): Risk of Reduced Cardiorespiratory and Musculoskeletal Fitness; Risk of Spaceflight-Induced Bone Changes
Issue / consequence if out of range: Insufficient mechanical loading, leading to muscle and bone loss.
Operational impact: Strength falling below the 80% threshold and reduced task performance.

What to track: Power, speed, duration and heart-rate response during aerobic exercise
Target / threshold: No NASA numeric target; track training intensity
Monitoring source: CEVIS cycle ergometer and T2 treadmill
Related risk(s): Risk of Reduced Cardiorespiratory and Musculoskeletal Fitness
Issue / consequence if out of range: Inadequate aerobic stimulus and VO2max decline.
Operational impact: Fatigue during EVA and reduced endurance.

What to track: VO2max from periodic fitness tests or estimates
Target / threshold: At least 32.9 ml/min/kg for microgravity EVA; 36.5 for surface EVA; at least 80% of pre-mission
Monitoring source: CEVIS cycle ergometer and T2 treadmill
Related risk(s): Risk of Reduced Cardiorespiratory and Musculoskeletal Fitness
Issue / consequence if out of range: Aerobic deconditioning and inability to sustain EVA workloads.
Operational impact: Compromised EVA performance, fatigue and higher injury risk.

What to track: Deadlift and bench press relative to body weight; in-mission strength retention
Target / threshold: At least 80% of baseline in flight; pre-mission deadlift 1.3-1.6x body weight and bench press 0.8-1.0x
Cadence: Pre-mission; periodic in flight; 5-7 days after landing
Related risk(s): Risk of Reduced Cardiorespiratory and Musculoskeletal Fitness; Risk of Injury and Compromised Performance from Spacewalks
Issue / consequence if out of range: Loss of muscle strength and power, joint instability and fall risk.
Operational impact: Difficulty handling suits and tools, performing EVA and egressing in an emergency.

What to track: BMD of total hip, lumbar spine and femoral neck by DXA
Target / threshold: Hip and spine at least 95% of pre-mission; femoral neck at least 90%
Related risk(s): Risk of Spaceflight-Induced Bone Changes
Related countermeasure(s): Resistive exercise for bone; Bisphosphonate medication
Issue / consequence if out of range: Bone loss, fractures and premature osteoporosis; hypercalciuria and kidney stones.
Operational impact: Fracture risk during landing or surface operations; renal stone event.

What to track: Calories consumed versus estimated expenditure
Target / threshold: Match intake to expenditure; no numeric NASA intake standard in reviewed sources
Related risk(s): Risk of Inadequate Food and Nutrition
Related countermeasure(s): Crew menu tasting and selection; Nutritionally enhanced diets
Issue / consequence if out of range: Weight loss, muscle wasting, fatigue, immune suppression and poor recovery.
Operational impact: Performance decrement, illness and reduced countermeasure effectiveness.

What to track: Carbohydrate, protein and fat intake
Target / threshold: Monitor intake; no numeric NASA targets in reviewed sources
Related risk(s): Risk of Inadequate Food and Nutrition
Issue / consequence if out of range: Insufficient protein for muscle maintenance and poor energy availability.
Operational impact: Muscle loss and fatigue.

What to track: Vitamin D, omega-3 fatty acids, lutein and other micronutrients
Target / threshold: Vitamin D supplementation required; dose is program-defined; monitor other micronutrients periodically
Monitoring source: Food and diet logs; periodic laboratory samples
Related risk(s): Risk of Inadequate Food and Nutrition; Risk of Spaceflight-Induced Bone Changes
Issue / consequence if out of range: Bone loss from low vitamin D, immune dysfunction, and vision and cardiovascular effects.
Operational impact: Higher risk of fracture, infection and ocular changes.

What to track: Sodium content of the diet
Target / threshold: Reduced-sodium space food; no numeric target in reviewed sources
Related risk(s): Risk of Inadequate Food and Nutrition; Risk of Cardiovascular Adaptations
Issue / consequence if out of range: Excess sodium may contribute to cardiovascular and fluid-balance problems.
Operational impact: Cardiovascular risk and blood-pressure changes.

What to track: Meal acceptability ratings and menu variety
Target / threshold: More than 200 foods and beverages available aboard the ISS; rate meals to prevent menu fatigue
Related risk(s): Risk of Inadequate Food and Nutrition
Related countermeasure(s): Crew menu tasting and selection; Lower-sodium, varied space food
Issue / consequence if out of range: Menu fatigue, reduced intake and weight loss.
Operational impact: Inadequate nutrition and performance decline.

What to track: Self-reported boredom with the menu and food intake decline
Target / threshold: No numeric NASA limit; track trend
Related risk(s): Risk of Inadequate Food and Nutrition
Issue / consequence if out of range: Declining food intake and morale.
Operational impact: Nutritional deficits and lower crew morale.

What to track: Fluid consumed per day (water, beverages, foods)
Target / threshold: No NASA numeric intake standard in reviewed sources; app default 2-3 L/day to be set with the flight surgeon
Related risk(s): Risk of Spaceflight-Induced Bone Changes (renal stone risk); Risk of Cardiovascular Adaptations
Issue / consequence if out of range: Dehydration, orthostatic intolerance, fainting at landing, kidney-stone risk, fatigue and cognitive decline.
Operational impact: Syncope during landing or egress; renal stone event; reduced performance.
Notes: Dehydration can worsen orthostatic intolerance and renal stone risk.

What to track: Self-reported urine color or point-of-care specific gravity
Target / threshold: No NASA threshold; trend with the clinical team
Related risk(s): Risk of Spaceflight-Induced Bone Changes
Issue / consequence if out of range: Under-hydration or over-hydration.
Operational impact: Impaired thermoregulation and cardiovascular stability.

What to track: Potable water supply and quality monitoring
Target / threshold: Potable water must meet spacecraft water exposure guidelines
Issue / consequence if out of range: Gastrointestinal infection or chemical exposure.
Operational impact: Crew illness and mission impact.
Notes: Quality monitoring covers chemical and microbiological safety.

What to track: Hypercalciuria and other urine markers
Target / threshold: No numeric NASA threshold; monitor alongside bone health
Related risk(s): Risk of Spaceflight-Induced Bone Changes
Issue / consequence if out of range: Kidney stone formation.
Operational impact: Severe pain and a medical event that may affect the mission.
Notes: Bone loss raises calcium excretion and kidney-stone risk.

What to track: Daily mood rating
Target / threshold: No NASA numeric limit; track trend against personal baseline
Related risk(s): Risk of Behavioral Changes and Psychiatric Disorders
Related countermeasure(s): Self-care including journaling; Virtual contact with family and medical staff
Issue / consequence if out of range: Depression, anxiety, low morale, and sleep and appetite changes.
Operational impact: Impaired decision-making, teamwork and mission performance.

What to track: Perceived stress rating
Target / threshold: No NASA numeric limit; track trend
Related risk(s): Risk of Behavioral Changes and Psychiatric Disorders
Issue / consequence if out of range: Cognitive impairment, sleep disruption, and cardiovascular and immune effects.
Operational impact: Errors, fatigue and conflict.

What to track: Perceived workload and task pressure
Target / threshold: No NASA numeric limit; track trend
Related risk(s): Risk of Behavioral Changes and Psychiatric Disorders; Risk of Inadequate Systems Operations Support
Issue / consequence if out of range: Fatigue, burnout and stress.
Operational impact: Performance decrement and safety risk.

What to track: Subjective sleepiness and fatigue rating
Target / threshold: No NASA numeric limit; track trend and task timing
Related risk(s): Risk from Inadequate Sleep and Irregular Schedules
Issue / consequence if out of range: Attention lapses and slowed reaction time.
Operational impact: Critical-task errors, especially during EVA and docking.

What to track: Team check-in and conflict indicators
Target / threshold: No NASA numeric limit; track trend
Related risk(s): Risk of Inadequate Teamwork
Issue / consequence if out of range: Conflict, miscommunication and reduced cohesion.
Operational impact: Mission performance and safety decrement.

What to track: Perceived privacy, isolation and contact with family
Target / threshold: No NASA numeric limit; track trend
Related risk(s): Risk of Behavioral Changes and Psychiatric Disorders; Risk of Inadequate Teamwork
Related countermeasure(s): Virtual contact with family and medical staff; Privacy-maximizing habitat design
Issue / consequence if out of range: Isolation distress, homesickness, and sleep and mood problems.
Operational impact: Morale and performance decline.

What to track: Reaction time, memory, attention and executive function
Target / threshold: Compare with personal pre-mission baseline
Related risk(s): Risk of Behavioral Changes and Psychiatric Disorders; Risk of Inadequate Systems Operations Support
Issue / consequence if out of range: Decline in attention, memory and reaction time.
Operational impact: Decision-making errors and safety risk.

What to track: Journaling, relaxation and recreation practice
Target / threshold: No numeric target; encourage daily practice
Related risk(s): Risk of Behavioral Changes and Psychiatric Disorders
Related countermeasure(s): Self-care including journaling; Designated relaxation and self-care time
Issue / consequence if out of range: Burnout, poor coping and psychological decline.
Operational impact: Reduced resilience and performance.

What to track: Structured body-system symptom report with severity and duration
Target / threshold: No numeric threshold; structured reporting and escalation
Related risk(s): Risk of Altered Immune System Responses; Risk of Host-Microorganism Interactions; Risk of Hypoxia
Related countermeasure(s): Biological sample monitoring for latent viruses
Issue / consequence if out of range: Undetected infection, immune alteration or other medical condition.
Operational impact: Progression to serious illness and mission impact.

What to track: Blurring, visual field changes, flashes or distortion
Target / threshold: Any new visual change triggers a same-day ocular check (app default)
Related risk(s): Risk of Spaceflight Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome (SANS)
Related countermeasure(s): Eye-protective nutritional supplements; Mechanical interventions for headward fluid shift
Issue / consequence if out of range: SANS with optic nerve swelling, retinal folds and brain swelling; possible long-term vision loss.
Operational impact: Visual performance decrement and long-term health risk.

What to track: Neurological symptoms and timing
Target / threshold: Red flag for hypoxia or CO2 exposure; check cabin oxygen and CO2 (app default)
Related risk(s): Risk of Hypoxia
Issue / consequence if out of range: Hypoxia or CO2 toxicity with cognitive impairment.
Operational impact: Incapacitation risk and task errors.

What to track: Joint pain, skin mottling or other pressure-related symptoms after a spacewalk
Target / threshold: Red flag for decompression sickness; follow the spacewalk abort protocol (app default)
Related risk(s): Risk of Decompression Sickness
Related countermeasure(s): Prebreathe oxygen protocols; Spacewalk abort and repressurization protocol
Issue / consequence if out of range: Decompression sickness, tissue damage and, in severe cases, stroke-like symptoms.
Operational impact: Medical emergency during or after a spacewalk.

What to track: Rashes, cold sores and other skin or viral signs
Target / threshold: Report for review; may indicate immune alteration or latent virus reactivation
Related risk(s): Risk of Altered Immune System Responses; Risk of Host-Microorganism Interactions
Related countermeasure(s): Biological sample monitoring for latent viruses; Pre-launch exposure restriction
Issue / consequence if out of range: Immune alteration, latent virus reactivation and infection.
Operational impact: Crew illness and reduced performance.

What to track: Nausea, diarrhea, constipation and appetite change
Target / threshold: Report for review; may relate to nutrition or microbiome changes
Related risk(s): Risk of Host-Microorganism Interactions; Risk of Inadequate Food and Nutrition
Issue / consequence if out of range: Infection, microbiome disturbance or malabsorption.
Operational impact: Illness and nutrition deficit.

What to track: Musculoskeletal pain, sprains or injuries
Target / threshold: Report for review; track cause and recovery
Related risk(s): Risk of Injury and Compromised Performance from Spacewalks; Risk of Injury from Dynamic Loads
Related countermeasure(s): Improved spacesuit design; Seat and restraint design standards
Issue / consequence if out of range: Musculoskeletal injury, pain and impaired mobility.
Operational impact: Reduced task performance; EVA and landing risk.

What to track: Dose, indication, adherence and side effects
Target / threshold: Log every use; review side effects with the flight surgeon
Related risk(s): Risk from Inadequate Sleep and Irregular Schedules; Risk of Behavioral Changes and Psychiatric Disorders
Issue / consequence if out of range: Side effects, drug interactions, impaired sleep or cognition, and dependence.
Operational impact: Performance and safety risk.
Notes: Includes sleep aids, caffeine, painkillers and vitamin D.
